content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "It is widely accepted that an important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: The important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn

modelEssay.title: The important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn
modelEssay.content:
It is widely accepted that an important goal of education is to help students learn how to learn. This concept emphasizes the development of lifelong learning skills rather than merely acquiring specific knowledge. In the era of rapid technological advancement, the ability to adapt and learn new things is crucial.

For instance, the internet has made vast amounts of information accessible, but it also requires individuals to sift through and discern credible sources. Students equipped with effective learning strategies are better positioned to navigate this digital landscape. Moreover, the ability to learn independently is essential for personal and professional growth. Personal experiences, such as mastering a new language or skill, often require self-directed learning and perseverance.

In conclusion, fostering a love for learning and teaching students how to learn is not just about academic success; it is about empowering individuals to continually grow and adapt in a changing world.

transcript.text: Conversation 1
transcript.translation: 对话一

transcript.text: Have you decided what you wish to study?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你想好要学什么了吗？

transcript.text: Yes, Professor.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 想好了，教授。

transcript.text: I wish to study architecture.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我想学建筑学。

transcript.text: Ah, that's a wonderful profession.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 啊，那是个很棒的职业。

transcript.text: Why did you choose it?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你为什么选择它？

transcript.text: I gave a lot of thought to things you said during our last discussion, and I decided architecture made the most sense for me.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我认真思考了上次讨论时您说的那些话，最后认定建筑学对我来说最合适。

transcript.text: In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 尤其是，我被设计与工程的结合所吸引。

transcript.text: That's great, but I seem to remember you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 很好，不过我记得你之前一直担心那些高深的数学。

transcript.text: You no longer think this aspect will be too hard for you?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你现在不觉得这方面对你来说太难了吗？

transcript.text: No, I was doing some online research, and I think I should be able to manage.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 不觉得了，我在网上查了些资料，我想我应该能应付得来。

transcript.text: Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 数学可能是课程中我会遇到的最难的科目，但我就是肯下所需要的功夫。

transcript.text: I'm certain the fruits of my labour will pay off.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我相信我的付出会有回报。

transcript.text: I'm sure that's true.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我相信确实如此。

transcript.text: Due to its material nature, architecture is one field where you'll be able to clearly witness the contribution you make to a city, and the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 由于建筑具有实体性，在这个领域里你能清楚地看到自己对一座城市的贡献，而你所留下的作品会比我们这些凡人存在得久远得多。

transcript.text: Yeah, I guess that's true too.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是啊，我想这话也没错。

transcript.text: So what subjects do you think I should start brushing up on in preparation?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那您觉得我该先温习哪些科目来做准备呢？

transcript.text: I have the whole summer.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我有一整个暑假。

transcript.text: These days, architecture is a very diverse and dynamic degree.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 如今建筑学是一个非常多元、非常有活力的专业。

transcript.text: Most universities will encourage you to learn different things from fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 大多数大学都会鼓励你去学习哲学、经济学等各种不同领域的知识。

transcript.text: Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science, because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不过，我建议你从计算机科学入手，因为你在做项目时需要制作大量复杂的视觉图形。

transcript.text: Any software in particular you think I should start with?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 您觉得我应该先从哪个软件学起？

transcript.text: Photoshop is a good place.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: Photoshop 是个不错的起点。

transcript.text: If you aren't yet, try to become as proficient as you can with it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 如果你还不熟练，就尽量把它练到精通。

transcript.text: And another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 另外我还建议你尽可能多学一些美术方面的知识。

transcript.text: In particular, the history of Western art.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 尤其是西方艺术史。

questions.questionText: Why does the woman wish to study architecture?

options.label: B

questions.analysis: 女士承认数学可能是课程中最难的科目，但表示「I'll simply put in the work required. I'm certain the fruits of my labour will pay off」，即靠下功夫、付出努力来克服。故选 A。C 的 online research 是她此前查资料评估难度，不是克服困难的办法。

questions.analysis: 教授说「the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals」，即建筑师留下的作品比人的寿命长久得多，对应 B 的 long-lasting。原文说的是 material nature（有形性），C 的 immaterial 与之相反；D 的 immortal（不朽、永生）夸大了 last much longer 的程度。

questions.questionText: What subject does the man suggest the woman start with?

options.label: B

transcript.text: So as I mentioned over the phone, we are looking for someone who is very discreet.

transcript.text: Thanks.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 谢谢。

transcript.text: I understand this too.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这一点我也明白。

transcript.text: This is my first job after graduating from university, so frankly I don't have much prior working experience.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这是我大学毕业后的第一份工作，坦白说我没有多少以往的工作经验。

transcript.text: I am however very excited about the prospect of joining this company and very keen to start from the bottom in whatever capacity I may be of use.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不过我对加入贵公司这件事非常期待，也很愿意从底层做起，在任何我能派上用场的岗位上工作。

transcript.text: That's good to hear.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 很高兴听你这么说。

transcript.text: You sound very energetic.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你听起来很有干劲。

transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 告诉我，你为什么认为自己很适合这份工作？

transcript.text: Well firstly, I love football.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 首先，我热爱足球。

transcript.text: I'm a lifelong Real Madrid supporter and go to their games every weekend I can.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我是皇家马德里的终身球迷，只要有可能，每个周末都会去看他们的比赛。

transcript.text: I would simply love to have a job where I'm involved in some capacity with Real Madrid, regardless of the position and salary.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我非常想有一份能以某种方式与皇马产生联系的工作，不论职位和薪水如何。

transcript.text: And secondly, I think what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool and I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 其次，我觉得贵公司在体育咨询方面所做的事情非常棒，而且我认为我的语言能力今后会很有用。

questions.analysis: 女士说「being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed」，high public profile 即公众知名度高，故选 C。D 把 player（球员）错记为 coach（教练）；A 的 occasionally 与「不被认出就出不了门」的程度不符。

questions.analysis: 女士说「As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common, everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez」，即受聘后担任桑切斯的私人助理。C 是干扰项：跑腿的对象是 Mr. Sanchez，不是 the woman（面试官）。故选 A。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 短文一。

transcript.text: Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing and mountain biking thus have lots of appeal.
transcript.translation: 因此，攀岩、冲浪、滑雪和山地自行车这类运动很有吸引力。

transcript.text: They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.
transcript.translation: 它们没有传统团队运动那么多的规则和压力，却同样具备户外体育活动的全部益处。

transcript.text: When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life.
transcript.translation: 在得到恰当监督的情况下，极限运动可以成为健康、均衡生活的一部分。

transcript.text: Some adventure sports may be associated with high risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks and when not to.
transcript.translation: 有些冒险运动可能伴随较高的受伤风险，因此孩子们弄清楚何时该冒险、何时不该冒险很重要。

transcript.text: Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears.
transcript.translation: 毫无风险的活动会剥夺孩子考验自己、克服恐惧的机会。

transcript.text: But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice.
transcript.translation: 但在一些人看来，正是这些风险使这类运动成为糟糕的选择。

transcript.text: They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.
transcript.translation: 他们说极限运动常常会导致严重的伤害，尤其是年轻的刺激追求者可能会尝试超出自己能力的高难度动作。

transcript.text: But let's be real.
transcript.translation: 但我们现实一点。

transcript.text: Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not.
transcript.translation: 不管你愿不愿意，大多数孩子都会去做各种危险的事。

transcript.text: Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children.
transcript.translation: 冒险运动有许多同样的风险和危险，但它们还额外带来冒险精神、勇气和自主性，而这些正是幼儿身上需要培养的。

transcript.text: As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids.
transcript.translation: 一如既往，什么对孩子最好要由家长来决定。

transcript.text: But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives.
transcript.translation: 但如果你确实认为冒险运动有点过头了，那就务必尝试把其他形式的户外冒险引入他们的生活。

transcript.text: Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.
transcript.translation: 露天野营、钓鱼、观星，甚至只是在树林里玩耍，都能极大地帮助孩子建立起与冒险运动同样的自信心和冒险意识。

transcript.text: Question 9.
transcript.translation: 问题 9。

transcript.text: Why do extreme sports appeal to many kids?
transcript.translation: 极限运动为什么吸引许多孩子？

transcript.text: Question 10.
transcript.translation: 问题 10。

transcript.text: What does the speaker say about risk-free activities?
transcript.translation: 关于毫无风险的活动，说话者说了什么？

transcript.text: Question 11.
transcript.translation: 问题 11。

transcript.text: What should parents do if they decide adventure sports are a bit too much for their kids?
transcript.translation: 如果家长认为冒险运动对孩子来说有点过头，他们该怎么做？

questions.questionText: Why do extreme sports appeal to many kids?

options.label: A
options.text: They bring more benefits to young people.

options.label: B
options.text: They require less supervision and training.

options.label: C
options.text: They are more suitable to young people.

options.label: D
options.text: They have fewer rules and pressures.

questions.analysis: 短文开头指出攀岩、冲浪、滑雪、山地自行车等运动很有吸引力，原因是「They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity」，即规则和压力少，故选 D。A 把「同样具有户外运动的益处」偷换成「益处更多」。

questions.questionText: What does the speaker say about risk-free activities?

options.label: A
options.text: They prevent kids from enjoying adventure sports.

options.label: B
options.text: They help kids guard against any possible injuries.

options.label: C
options.text: They rob kids of the chance to cultivate their courage.

options.label: D
options.text: They deprive kids of the opportunity to develop team spirit.

questions.analysis: 原文「Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears」，即无风险活动剥夺了孩子考验自己、克服恐惧的机会，克服恐惧即培养勇气，故选 C。D 把 overcome their fears 偷换成 develop team spirit。

questions.questionText: What should parents do if they decide adventure sports are a bit too much for their kids?

options.label: A
options.text: Help them take up these sports when they are more mature.

options.label: B
options.text: Let them participate in some less risky outdoor activities.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask them to try some forms of indoor sports.

options.label: D
options.text: Introduce them to these sports step by step.

questions.analysis: 结尾建议「if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives」，并举例露营、钓鱼、观星、在树林里玩，都是风险较低的户外活动，故选 B。C 的 indoor（室内）与原文 outdoor 相反；D 是「循序渐进地引导他们做这些极限运动」，与「改做别的活动」不同。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 短文二。

transcript.text: The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow.
transcript.translation: 今天光鲜亮丽的电子产品，明天就会变成垃圾。

transcript.text: Manufacturers don't talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing.
transcript.translation: 厂商在发布那些用来取代你手中其实同样好用的旧产品的新品时，对此几乎只字不提。

transcript.text: In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired, so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.
transcript.translation: 事实上，科技公司常常故意把设备设计成寿命不长且无法维修，这样消费者就不得不掏钱买新的。

transcript.text: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score.
transcript.translation: 今年，法国政府开始要求科技厂商标注可维修性评分。

transcript.text: If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets.
transcript.translation: 如果一台设备可以维修，它的寿命就能延长，既为消费者省钱，也让地球免于承受如此多废弃电子产品的负担。

transcript.text: Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.
transcript.translation: 掌握了这些信息，消费者就能更好地选择该买哪些产品。

transcript.text: Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year.
transcript.translation: 每年约有 5900 万吨废旧电视、电脑、显示屏、智能手机、洗衣机等电子产品被丢弃。

transcript.text: This waste is dangerous.
transcript.translation: 这些垃圾很危险。

transcript.text: Batteries explode in recycling facilities.
transcript.translation: 电池会在回收设施中爆炸。

transcript.text: Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air.
transcript.translation: 汞等有毒物质会渗入土壤和地下水，并扩散到空气中。

transcript.text: Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
transcript.translation: 制造平板显示屏会向大气中排放温室气体。

transcript.text: We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem.
transcript.translation: 我们需要科技公司带头解决这个问题。

transcript.text: If they won't, governments must make them do so.
transcript.translation: 如果它们不愿意，政府就必须迫使它们这样做。

transcript.text: Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits.
transcript.translation: 尽管科技公司常把环境可持续性挂在嘴边，许多公司却在游说反对维修立法，担心这会侵蚀它们的利润。

transcript.text: Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies.
transcript.translation: 可持续性固然重要，但对这些公司来说，好卖的设计似乎更重要。

transcript.text: Consumers should support right to repair legislation.
transcript.translation: 消费者应当支持维修权立法。

transcript.text: In this world, damage is a certainty, but we cannot leave things broken.
transcript.translation: 在这个世界上，损坏是必然的，但我们不能任由东西一直坏着。

transcript.text: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
transcript.translation: 我们自己造成的问题，是可以解决的问题。

questions.questionText: What should tech companies do to help ensure environmental sustainability?

options.label: D

questions.questionText: What does the speaker think of the problem of waste?

transcript.text: Recording 1.
transcript.translation: 录音一。

transcript.text: On average, US workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online.
transcript.translation: 美国员工平均把大约百分之十的工作时间花在上网、给朋友发邮件或网购上。

transcript.text: This behaviour, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.
transcript.translation: 这种被称为「网络摸鱼」的行为，据信每年让雇主损失高达 850 亿美元的生产力。

transcript.text: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behaviour through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies.
transcript.translation: 大多数关于网络摸鱼的研究，关注的是如何通过网络监控、电脑使用规定等干预手段来阻止员工做出这种行为。

transcript.text: But it turns out such behaviour may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time.
transcript.translation: 但事实表明，这种行为未必说明员工懒惰或只是在浪费时间。

transcript.text: Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction.
transcript.translation: 工作中使用社交媒体已被发现与更高的员工投入度和工作满意度相关。

transcript.text: New research suggests cyberloafing could help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.
transcript.translation: 新的研究表明，网络摸鱼可能有助于员工应对压力极大的工作环境。

transcript.text: But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels?
transcript.translation: 但网络摸鱼真的能有效降低员工的压力水平吗？

transcript.text: That's the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study.
transcript.translation: 这正是我的研究团队在新研究中想要回答的问题。

transcript.text: Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations.
transcript.translation: 我们的假设是，网络摸鱼可以充当一种短暂的休息，让员工有机会从压力大的工作情境中恢复过来。

transcript.text: To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non-work emails and shopping.
transcript.translation: 为了验证这一点，我们请员工填写一份在线问卷，对自己花在网络摸鱼、查看非工作邮件和购物上的时间进行评估。

transcript.text: We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at.
transcript.translation: 我们还请他们对工作满意度、离职意愿以及在职场遭受不公对待（比如被欺负、威胁或呵斥）的频率进行评分。

transcript.text: As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit.
transcript.translation: 正如你可能预料到的，我们发现总体而言，职场中遭受的不公对待越多，工作满意度越低，离职意愿越强。

transcript.text: More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection.
transcript.translation: 更有意思的是，我们发现网络摸鱼有效地缓冲了这种关联。

transcript.text: That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn't cyberloaf as much.
transcript.translation: 也就是说，与摸鱼较少的同类参与者相比，那些遭受不公对待但花更多时间上网和查邮件的员工，工作满意度更高，离职意愿也更低。

transcript.text: This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.
transcript.translation: 这表明网络摸鱼对员工而言相当于一个减压阀，帮助他们从有压力的经历中恢复。

transcript.text: While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress, it may not only reduce worker turnover but also ultimately bolster productivity.
transcript.translation: 虽然我们没有直接评估网络摸鱼如何影响员工绩效，但我们认为，通过缓解压力，它不仅可能降低员工流失率，最终还可能提升生产率。

transcript.text: This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance.
transcript.translation: 这与近期另一些研究的结论一致：短暂休息与更高的日常工作绩效相关。

transcript.text: That isn't to say cyberloafing is always good.
transcript.translation: 这并不是说网络摸鱼总是好事。

transcript.text: Too much time spent on non-work activities likely causes performance to suffer.
transcript.translation: 在非工作活动上花太多时间很可能会损害绩效。

transcript.text: All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees.
transcript.translation: 总的来说，管理者对员工应当更宽容一些。

transcript.text: We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.
transcript.translation: 我们认为，在工作中稍微网购或上上网，从长远看能让员工更有效率。

options.label: A

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

transcript.text: Recording 2.
transcript.translation: 录音二。

transcript.text: When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory.
transcript.translation: 1854 年朱利叶斯·莫顿搬到内布拉斯加城时，他面临着该地区许多定居者共同的问题。

transcript.text: It was a treeless plain.
transcript.translation: 那是一片没有树木的平原。

transcript.text: That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel.
transcript.translation: 这意味着没有树木可作建筑材料，也没有树木可作燃料。

transcript.text: But Morton was one of the world's first conservationists, stating, For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed.
transcript.translation: 但莫顿是世界上最早的环保主义者之一，他表示：为了繁荣，我们消耗掉多少森林，就应当种回多少森林。

transcript.text: So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land.
transcript.translation: 于是他开始种树，先从自己的土地种起。

transcript.text: By 1860, Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees.
transcript.translation: 到 1860 年，莫顿已拥有一片三百多棵树的树林。

transcript.text: A few years later, he had more than 1,000.
transcript.translation: 几年之后，他种下的树超过了一千棵。

transcript.text: As the forests grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska.
transcript.translation: 随着林木不断长大，莫顿在内布拉斯加州的影响力也随之增长。

transcript.text: This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting.
transcript.translation: 这在很大程度上是因为莫顿创办了该州第一份报纸《内布拉斯加城新闻报》，并经常在报上撰写社论，阐述植树在实用和审美方面的好处。

transcript.text: He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture.
transcript.translation: 他还组建了内布拉斯加州园艺协会，并在该州农业委员会任职。

transcript.text: While serving on the board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.
transcript.translation: 在委员会任职期间，莫顿想出了一个把植树理念推广到全州的办法。

transcript.text: On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated Day for the Planting of Trees in the State of Nebraska, and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves.
transcript.translation: 1872 年 1 月 4 日，莫顿起草了一项决议，提议将 4 月 10 日定为内布拉斯加州植树日，并号召人们走出家门亲手植树。

transcript.text: Morton called the special event Arbor Day, as arbor is Latin for tree.
transcript.translation: 莫顿把这个特别的日子称为 Arbor Day，因为 arbor 在拉丁语中意为「树」。

transcript.text: The state government agreed, and on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska.
transcript.translation: 州政府表示同意，1872 年 4 月 10 日，第一个非官方的植树节在内布拉斯加州各地举行。

transcript.text: Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees.
transcript.translation: 植树数量最多的县、市和个人都获得了奖励。

transcript.text: That day, an astounding 1 million trees were planted in Nebraska, an average of more than six for every man, woman, and child in the state.
transcript.translation: 那一天，内布拉斯加州种下了惊人的一百万棵树，相当于全州每位男女老少平均种了六棵以上。

transcript.text: Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname the Tree Planter's State.
transcript.translation: 自 1885 年以来，内布拉斯加州已植树逾七十万英亩，因而获得了「植树者之州」的绰号。

transcript.text: Arbor Day became a legal civic holiday in the state in 1885.
transcript.translation: 1885 年，植树节成为该州法定的公民假日。

transcript.text: It was held on April 22, Julius Morton's birthday.
transcript.translation: 节日定在 4 月 22 日，也就是朱利叶斯·莫顿的生日。

transcript.text: In addition to a parade in Nebraska City, Morton introduced what has since become a long-standing Arbor Day tradition.
transcript.translation: 除了在内布拉斯加城举行游行外，莫顿还开创了一项此后长期延续的植树节传统。

transcript.text: Schoolchildren went outside and planted trees together.
transcript.translation: 学童们走到户外，一起种树。

transcript.text: In 1970, nearly a century after Arbor Day was first celebrated, President Richard Nixon declared the last Friday of every April to be observed as National Arbor Day.
transcript.translation: 1970 年，也就是首次庆祝植树节将近一个世纪之后，理查德·尼克松总统宣布将每年 4 月的最后一个星期五定为全国植树节。

transcript.text: All 50 states recognize the April observance, although many hold an additional State Arbor Day in a month more suited to local tree planting.
transcript.translation: 全部五十个州都承认这一四月的节日，不过许多州还会在更适合当地植树的月份另设一个州植树节。

transcript.translation: 朱利叶斯·莫顿做了什么，使他在内布拉斯加城的影响力得以提升？

transcript.text: Question 21.

questions.questionText: What does the speaker say about Nebraska City in 1854 when Julius Morton moved there?

questions.questionText: What did Julius Morton do that increased his influence in Nebraska City?

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

questions.questionText: What does the speaker say happened on April 10, 1872?

options.label: A
options.text: A special prize was awarded to Julius Morton.

options.label: B
options.text: One million trees were planted throughout Nebraska.

options.label: C
options.text: The state government declared it the official Arbor Day.

options.label: D
options.text: Nebraska earned the nickname "the Tree Planters State".

questions.analysis: 原文「on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska... That day, an astounding 1 million trees were planted in Nebraska」，故选 B。C 错在当天是 unofficial（非官方）；D 的绰号来自 1885 年后累计植树 70 万英亩；奖项是发给各县、市和个人，不是发给莫顿本人。

transcript.text: Recording 3.
transcript.translation: 录音三。

transcript.text: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 现代人类大约在二十万年前起源于非洲。

transcript.text: They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 随后在距今六万年之后的某个时候，他们扩散到欧洲和亚洲各地。

transcript.text: This is the out-of-Africa model, as it's commonly known.
transcript.translation: 这就是人们通常所说的「走出非洲」模型。

transcript.text: In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance, but this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.
transcript.translation: 20 世纪 90 年代，这一假说被广泛接受，但这个流行的观点需要修正，尤其是考虑到过去几十年间亚洲各地的大量重要发现。

transcript.text: For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years.
transcript.translation: 例如，新发现的许多人类化石——尤其是在中国发现的——如今测定的年代都早于六万年。

transcript.text: This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 这就对「现代人类直到六万年前才走出非洲」这一观点提出了质疑。

transcript.text: Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna Cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
transcript.translation: 以近期在中国广西壮族自治区娄洞发现的两颗现代人牙齿为例。

transcript.text: When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old, a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
transcript.translation: 当我和研究团队对这两颗牙齿进行年代测定时，发现它们已有七万多年历史；如果现代人类六万年前才走出非洲，这种情况显然不可能出现。

transcript.text: So with such findings, what happened exactly?
transcript.translation: 那么面对这些发现，究竟发生了什么？

transcript.text: Where does the most current data suggest we came from?
transcript.translation: 最新的数据表明我们究竟来自哪里？

transcript.text: The first question we should ask is, why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with?
transcript.translation: 我们首先该问的问题是：现代人类当初为什么要离开非洲？

transcript.text: If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change.
transcript.translation: 如果一个种群完全适应了某个特定环境，并且能够获得充足的资源，那么它其实没有理由迁移或改变。

transcript.text: For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
transcript.translation: 例如，非洲的一些猴子，其牙齿在数百万年间几乎没有变化，这表明它们找到了一处适合自己的地方。

transcript.text: So what happened with humans?
transcript.translation: 那么人类身上发生了什么？

transcript.text: Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands.
transcript.translation: 一些研究者认为，人口密度增长到了迫使较小的人群去开拓新土地的程度。

transcript.text: Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures.
transcript.translation: 另一些研究者认为，由于东非发生了重大的环境事件，人类被迫去寻找更肥美的土地。

transcript.text: Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realising that they were actually moving from one continent to another.
transcript.translation: 还有一种解释可能仅仅是：早期现代人猎手在追随他们赖以为生的大型动物，于是走出了非洲，却没有意识到自己其实正从一个大陆迁往另一个大陆。

transcript.text: Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas.
transcript.translation: 人类每天都需要可靠的淡水，而许多沿海地区似乎并不具备这一条件。

transcript.text: This brings us to another question, by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?
transcript.translation: 这就引出了另一个问题：现代人类是沿哪条路线走出非洲的？

transcript.text: No clear routes across the Mediterranean from North Africa appear to be present.
transcript.translation: 从北非跨越地中海的路线似乎并不明确存在。

transcript.text: So the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.
transcript.translation: 因此，早期走出非洲、进入欧洲和亚洲的扩散过程，可能是经由阿拉伯半岛完成的。

While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study __27__ how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next. Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically __28__ every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio. These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to __29__ how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day. The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two __30__ weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.
paragraphs.translation: 你可能没有你想象的那么了解自己。根据一项新研究，人们只对自己某些行为的判断相对准确。尽管大多数关于人们自我认知的先前研究都集中在长期人格特质上，但这项新研究探讨了人们如何理解自己从一刻到下一刻的行为。研究人员要求参与者佩戴音频记录器，该记录器在早上7点到凌晨2点之间每9.5分钟自动激活，录制30秒的音频。这些参与者每天被发送四次调查问卷，询问他们回忆在一天中的特定小时内外向、随和或认真尽责的程度。该研究使用了248名参与者的数据，所有参与者都连续两周回答了关于他们行为的问题，并在其中一周佩戴了音频设备。

paragraphs.text: Six laboratory assistants rated each participant's audio clips to see how their observations compared with people's __31__ of themselves. The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted. Further, participants' ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers' for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being. But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. Some of this __32__ could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read __33__ like body language, but there are __34__ other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude. The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather __35__ rude behavior.
paragraphs.translation: 六名实验室助手评估了每位参与者的音频片段，以比较他们的观察与人们的自我评估。这六名助手对他们观察的人的行为大体上达成一致。此外，参与者对自己行为的评分与观察者在评估外向性和认真尽责方面一致。但参与者和外部观察者在随和性方面的共识要小得多。这种差异的部分原因可能是因为观察者仅使用音频片段，因此无法读取肢体语言等线索，但可能还有其他解释，因为人们应该能听到参与者何时友善何时粗鲁。参与者自认为的行为与观察者所听到的之间的低共识可能是因为人们更愿意否认粗鲁行为。

questionGroups.title: Why we need tiny colleges

paragraphs.text: We're experiencing the rebirth of smallness. Farmers markets, tiny homes, and brew pubs all exemplify our love of smallness. So do charter schools, coffee shops, and local bookstores. Small is often (but not always) more affordable, healthier, and sustainable, but its finest characteristic, the one that turns charm into love, is that going small allows us to be more fully who we are.
paragraphs.translation: 我们正在经历小型化的复兴。农贸市场、小型住宅和精酿酒吧都体现了我们对小型事物的热爱。特许学校、咖啡店和本地书店也是如此。小型往往（但并非总是）更实惠、更健康、更可持续，但其最美好的特质——将魅力转化为爱——在于选择小型化能让我们更充分地做自己。

paragraphs.text: In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction: Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered "mid-sized". The nation's largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. At the other end of the spectrum is a handful of colleges that have fewer than a hundred students on campus and no online courses: colleges such as Sterling College, Thomas More College of Liberal Arts, and Deep Springs College. These colleges are so small that they can only be called "tiny."
paragraphs.translation: 在高等教育中，趋势大多相反：拥有两万或三万学生的大学被视为“中等规模”。全国最大的大学亚利桑那州立大学在校生有八万人，并计划在线招收另外十万人。在另一端，有一些学院在校生不足百人，且没有在线课程：例如斯特林学院、托马斯莫尔文理学院和深泉学院。这些学院如此之小，只能被称为“微型”。

paragraphs.text: Tiny colleges focus not just on a young person's intellect, but on the young person as a whole. Equally important, tiny colleges ask, "How can education contribute to human flourishing and the well-being of the world?" And they shape a college experience to address that question. They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities.
paragraphs.translation: 微型学院不仅关注年轻人的智力，还关注年轻人的整体发展。同样重要的是，微型学院会问：“教育如何能促进人类的繁荣和世界的福祉？”他们塑造大学体验来回答这个问题。他们用对学生作为社区全面发展成员的成长关注，取代了对机构发展的担忧。

paragraphs.text: I've had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career-a small liberal arts college and two mid-sized public universities. I've also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions, and in many of my colleagues, especially when it comes to helping students and preparing them for the many responsibilities of adulthood. Administrators focus on the business of running a university, and most faculty focus on their scholarship and teaching their discipline. Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings.
paragraphs.translation: 在我的职业生涯中，我有幸在三所不同的高等教育机构任教——一所小型文理学院和两所中等规模的公立大学。我也对这些机构以及我的许多同事深感失望，尤其是在帮助学生并为他们成年后的诸多责任做准备方面。管理者专注于大学的运营事务，大多数教职员工专注于他们的学术研究和学科教学。很少有人刻意关注学生作为个体和社会成员的成熟过程。

paragraphs.text: Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I'm now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college—Flagstaff College. I'm convinced there's a need for another type of education, one devoted to helping students come into their own and into this beautiful and troubled world. Young people need an education that will provide them with meaning, hope, courage, and passion, as well as information and skills. Large institutions, I believe, are particularly ill-suited to this type of education.
paragraphs.translation: 刚从一所公立大学退休后，我正返回家乡亚利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫，去创建一所微型学院——弗拉格斯塔夫学院。我相信需要另一种类型的教育，一种致力于帮助学生找到自我并进入这个美丽而充满问题的世界的教育。年轻人需要一种能提供意义、希望、勇气和激情，以及信息和技能的教育。我认为大型机构特别不适合这种类型的教育。

paragraphs.text: There's no "best of" list when it comes to tiny colleges, at least not yet. But around the country people are creating new colleges that provide an alternative to small liberal arts colleges, large public universities, and online education.
paragraphs.translation: 关于微型学院，目前还没有“最佳”榜单，至少现在还没有。但全国各地的人们正在创建新的学院，为小型文理学院、大型公立大学和在线教育提供替代选择。

paragraphs.text: With only 26 students, Deep Springs is the smallest college in the country and, quite likely, the most atypical (非典型的). Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men, committed to educating students for "a life of service to humanity." Founded by the electricity tycoon (大亨) L.L. Nunn in 1917, Deep Springs "curriculum" revolved around academics, labor, and self-governance. In addition to their courses, students are charged with running the 155-acre ranch and overseeing the functioning of the college. Students chair both the admissions and the curriculum committees.
paragraphs.translation: 只有26名学生的深泉学院是全国最小的学院，也很可能是最非典型的。位于加利福尼亚州和内华达州交界处的一个运营中的养牛牧场，深泉学院是一所私立、寄宿制、为期两年的男子学院，致力于教育学生“为人类服务的人生”。由电力大亨L.L.努恩于1917年创立，深泉学院的“课程”围绕学术、劳动和自治展开。除了课程外，学生还负责管理155英亩的牧场并监督学院的运作。学生主持招生和课程委员会。

paragraphs.text: "Living in close community with one's teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one's growth as a person," says William Hunt, who graduated last year. "To exist for very long in a community like that, you have to get over the question of whether you're sufficiently talented or principled and get started worrying about how you can stretch yourself and your peers, how much you can manage to learn with them."
paragraphs.translation: “与老师和同学紧密生活在社区中，并被迫承担成人责任，这促进了个人的成长，”去年毕业的威廉·亨特说。“要在这样的社区中长期存在，你必须克服自己是否足够有才华或有原则的问题，并开始担心如何挑战自己和同伴，以及你能和他们一起学到多少。”

paragraphs.text: Sterling College, in Craftsbury Common, Vermont, is also very small-fewer than 100 students. Unlike Deep Springs, Sterling focuses its curriculum on environmental and social justice issues, but like Deep Springs it places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor. According to its catalog, a college education at Sterling combines "rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work."
paragraphs.translation: 位于佛蒙特州克拉夫茨伯里康芒的斯特林学院也非常小——学生不到100人。与深泉学院不同，斯特林学院的课程侧重于环境和社会正义问题，但像深泉学院一样，它高度重视个人责任和体力劳动。根据其目录，斯特林学院的大学教育结合了“严谨的学术、卷起袖子迎接的挑战和传统的辛勤工作。”

paragraphs.text: The average tuition at a small liberal-arts college is $30,000 to $40,000 a year, not including the cost of living on campus, as compared to $8,000 to $10,000 a year for tuition alone at a public university. Of the tiny colleges, only Deep Springs doesn't charge tuition or room and board; students pay only for books and the cost of traveling to and from college. If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable.
paragraphs.translation: 小型文理学院的平均学费为每年三万到四万美元，不包括校园生活费用，而公立大学的学费仅为每年八千到一万美元。在微型学院中，只有深泉学院不收学费或食宿费；学生只需支付书籍和往返学院的费用。如果微型学院要在高等教育领域占有一席之地，它们需要找到真正负担得起的方式。

paragraphs.text: Doing so may not be that difficult so long as they do not pattern themselves too closely on existing norms. We've come to believe that a good college should have many academic programs and excellent facilities, posh (豪华的) dorms, an array of athletic programs, and a world-class student activity center. Imagine a good college without a climbing wall! We also have accepted the idea that college presidents, and their many vice-presidents, should be paid like their counterparts in the business world and that higher education requires an elaborate, up-to-date technology infrastructure. All of this drives up the cost of education.
paragraphs.translation: 只要他们不过分模仿现有规范，这样做可能并不困难。我们逐渐相信一所好大学应该拥有许多学术项目和优秀的设施、豪华的宿舍、一系列体育项目和世界级的学生活动中心。想象一所没有攀岩墙的好大学！我们还接受了这样的观点：大学校长及其众多副校长应该像商业世界的同行一样获得报酬，高等教育需要一个精心设计、最新的技术基础设施。所有这些都推高了教育成本。

paragraphs.text: The "trick" to making tiny colleges affordable, if that's the right word, is simplicity. At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. Reflecting on his own college education, President Garfield once commented that an ideal college would consist of nothing more than the legendary teacher Mark Hopkins on one end of a log and a student on the other. The economics of a tiny college, in other words, might be similar to that of a tiny house. Because it is small, a tiny house costs less to build and less to furnish, insure, and maintain. But the economic benefits of a small house don't end there. Tiny homes discourage homeowners from buying stuff that they really don't need, because there's no place to put it.
paragraphs.translation: 让微型学院负担得起的“诀窍”，如果这个词合适的话，就是简约。教育的核心是人与人之间的互动。回顾自己的大学教育，加菲尔德校长曾经评论说，一所理想的大学不过是在一根原木的一端坐着传奇教师马克·霍普金斯，另一端坐着一个学生。换句话说，微型学院的经济可能类似于微型住宅。由于它小，微型住宅建造成本低，装饰、保险和维护成本也低。但小型住宅的经济效益不止于此。微型住宅不鼓励业主购买他们真正不需要的东西，因为没有地方放。

paragraphs.text: I'm a late convert to the idea of tiny colleges, and I fully understand the need for many diverse types of educational institutions. Academic research and job training are important, but tiny colleges aren't suited for either. The educational needs of a complex society are themselves complex, and no single model can meet all of these needs. But I'm now convinced there's an educational need that's now going almost completely unmet: namely, the need to help young people transition into adulthood. Tiny colleges can do this better than any other type of educational institution.
paragraphs.translation: 我是微型学院理念的后来皈依者，我完全理解需要多种类型的教育机构。学术研究和职业培训很重要，但微型学院两者都不适合。复杂社会的教育需求本身就是复杂的，没有单一模式能满足所有需求。但我现在确信有一个教育需求几乎完全未得到满足：即帮助年轻人过渡到成年的需求。微型学院能比任何其他类型的教育机构更好地做到这一点。

paragraphs.text: The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us, and that one of the basic purposes of higher education is social. Although we give lip service to the idea that a college education will make us better people, when all's said and done, we think of higher education primarily in economic terms. We've come to think of higher education as a means to make a living rather than make a life. We've also come to see higher education as a private good rather than a public one. Tiny colleges are not the answer to all of our educational requirements, but they're an answer to one of our most basic educational necessities; the need to produce thoughtful, engaged, and compassionate human beings.
paragraphs.translation: 微型学院的最终理由是坚信我们每个人通过与了解和关心我们的人密切互动来达到完整的人性，而高等教育的基本目的之一是社会性的。尽管我们口头上承认大学教育会让我们成为更好的人，但归根结底，我们主要从经济角度思考高等教育。我们已将高等教育视为谋生而非生活的手段。我们还将高等教育视为私人产品而非公共产品。微型学院并非能满足我们所有教育需求的答案，但它们是对我们最基本教育需求之一的回答；即培养深思熟虑、积极参与和富有同情心的人类。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: If you're someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the pandemic (大流行病), you're not alone. Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies' aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health. In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants' efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they're responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates.
paragraphs.translation: 如果你是在大流行病期间更多地转向吃垃圾食品的人，你并不孤单。调查记者迈克尔·莫斯说，加工食品被设计来让你上瘾，就像酒精、香烟或其他有害物质一样。他2013年的书《盐糖脂肪》探讨了食品公司对这些产品的激进营销及其对健康的影响。在他的新书《上瘾》中，莫斯更新了食品巨头们如何努力让我们继续吃他们提供的食物，以及他们如何回应消费者和健康倡导者的投诉。

paragraphs.text: Processed food is inexpensive, it's legal, and it's everywhere. Companies' advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly. So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people. Memory, nostalgia (怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave. Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they're at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment. Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they're going to think of soda. Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood.
paragraphs.translation: 加工食品价格低廉，合法，而且无处不在。公司的广告暗示我们记住那些产品，我们不断想要那些产品。因此，食物环境是使食物对许多人来说更成问题的关键因素之一。记忆，尤其是怀旧，在我们渴望的食物中扮演着重要角色。苏打水公司发现，如果他们在孩子与父母一起观看球赛时将苏打水递给孩子，那么这种苏打水将永远与那个快乐时刻相关联。在生活中，当那个孩子想要体验快乐时刻时，他们会想到苏打水。许多人从他们童年记忆中的零食中寻求安慰。

paragraphs.text: Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking.
paragraphs.translation: 莫斯审视了公司如何利用我们的记忆、渴望和大脑化学来让我们继续吃零食。

paragraphs.text: One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory. What we eat is all about memory. And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age. And we keep those memories for a lifetime. Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively. There's nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain. For Moss, this puts the notion of "fast food" in an entirely new light as this isn't limited to fast food chains-almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods. Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.
paragraphs.translation: 我之所以认为其中一些食品甚至比毒品更强大、更麻烦的原因之一是记忆。我们所吃的食物全都关乎记忆。我们在很小的年龄就开始形成对食物的记忆。我们一生都保留着这些记忆。知道这一点，食品行业花费大量时间试图塑造我们对其产品的记忆。研究药物成瘾的科学家在20世纪90年代发现的一个成瘾特征是，一种物质越快击中大脑，我们就越容易冲动行事。没有什么比食物在击中大脑的能力上更快的了。对莫斯来说，这使“快餐”的概念焕然一新，因为这不仅限于快餐连锁店——杂货店中几乎90%的食品都是加工食品。这个行业的一切都关于速度，从制造到包装。

paragraphs.text: Overall, Moss outlines the industry's dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers. Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.
paragraphs.translation: 总体而言，莫斯概述了该行业对制造价格低廉、超级美味且对消费者来说极其便利的产品的依赖。现在，越来越多的人关心他们摄入体内的东西并希望吃得更健康，这些公司发现自己很难满足这种新需求，因为他们自身对制作这些便利食品的成瘾。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Chimpanzees (黑猩猩), human beings' closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes. Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives. Fewer than 300,000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe. At more than 7 billion, the human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals—despite our physical weaknesses.
paragraphs.translation: 黑猩猩是人类最亲近的动物亲戚，共享我们高达98%的基因。然而，人类和黑猩猩过着截然不同的生活。如今，不到30万只野生黑猩猩生活在非洲的几个森林角落，而人类已经殖民了地球的每一个角落。人口超过70亿，人类数量使几乎所有其他哺乳动物相形见绌——尽管我们身体较弱。

paragraphs.text: What could account for our species' incredible evolutionary successes?
paragraphs.translation: 什么能解释我们物种令人难以置信的进化成功？

paragraphs.text: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe. But a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists (人类学家) are rejecting that explanation. They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don't think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.
paragraphs.translation: 一个明显的答案是我们拥有大脑。可能是我们的原始智力赋予我们前所未有的能力，能够跳出框框思考，在全球迁移过程中创新解决棘手问题。但越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家正在拒绝这种解释。他们认为，我们并非以创新为生，而是因为我们不独立思考才能生存和繁荣。相反，人们通过仔细模仿他人来应对挑战性的气候和生态环境。

paragraphs.text: In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects-children and chimpanzees-a mechanical box with a treat inside. In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent. The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick.
paragraphs.translation: 在一项著名研究中，心理学家维多利亚·霍纳和安德鲁·惠顿向两组测试对象——儿童和黑猩猩——展示了一个内有奖励的机械盒子。在一个条件下，盒子是不透明的，而在另一个条件下是透明的。实验者演示了如何打开盒子取出奖励，但他们也包括了一个不相关的步骤：用棍子敲击盒子。

paragraphs.text: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they'd witnessed.
paragraphs.translation: 奇怪的是，孩子们仔细模仿了打开盒子的所有步骤，即使他们能看到棍子没有实际作用。也就是说，他们非理性地模仿：孩子们不是只做获得奖励所必需的事情，而是盲目模仿他们目睹的每一个动作。

paragraphs.text: Of course, that study only included three- and four-year-olds. But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others' actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate—that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions.
paragraphs.translation: 当然，那项研究只包括三岁和四岁的儿童。但进一步的研究表明，年龄较大的儿童和成年人更有可能盲目模仿他人的行为，而婴儿则不太可能过度模仿——即精确模仿甚至不切实际的动作。

paragraphs.text: By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition. In the transparent condition-where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless-they ignored that step entirely. Other research has since supported these findings.
paragraphs.translation: 相比之下，研究中的黑猩猩只在不透明条件下过度模仿。在透明条件下——他们看到棍子在机械上无用——他们完全忽略了那个步骤。其他研究随后支持了这些发现。

paragraphs.text: When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults.
paragraphs.translation: 当涉及到模仿时，黑猩猩比人类儿童或成年人更理性。

paragraphs.text: Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from? Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.
paragraphs.translation: 这种看似非理性的人类对过度模仿的偏好从何而来？人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇指出，世界各地的人们依赖的技术往往如此复杂，以至于没有人能理性地学习它们。相反，人们必须逐步学习，信任更有经验的长辈和同伴的智慧。

paragraphs.text: So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. We're not chimpanzees, after all.
paragraphs.translation: 所以，下次当你听到有人激烈地争论每个人都应该拥抱非从众性并避免模仿他人时，你可能会笑一笑。毕竟，我们不是黑猩猩。

questionGroups.sourceText: 近年来,中国城市加快发展,城市人居环境得到显著改善。许多城市努力探索中国特色的城市高质量发展之路,城市功能不断完善,治理水平明显提高。中国持续开展城市生态修复和功能修补,全面实施城镇老旧小区改造,大力推进城市园林绿化,消除污染;同时大力推进城市基础设施体系化建设,开展房屋建筑和市政设施普查以及安全隐患排查整治,努力为市民创造高品质的生活环境,让城市更美丽、更安全、更宜居。

answer.modelTranslation: In recent years, Chinese cities have accelerated their development, leading to significant improvements in urban living environments. Many cities are striving to explore a high-quality development path with Chinese characteristics, with continuous improvements in urban functions and a noticeable enhancement in governance levels. China persists in urban ecological restoration and functional repair, fully implementing the renovation of old urban communities in towns, vigorously promoting urban greening and landscape, and eliminating pollution. At the same time, there is a strong push for the systematic construction of urban infrastructure, conducting surveys of housing and municipal facilities, and rectifying safety hazards, all in an effort to create a high-quality living environment for citizens, making cities more beautiful, safer, and more livable.
